title: Lopud with Toddlers & Kids: Family Travel Guide 2027
metaDescription: Lopud with toddlers: shallow sandy Šunj beach, car-free lanes, ferry from Dubrovnik in 45–55 min, golf carts at €3, where to stay and what to pack.
content:
## Why Lopud Works for Toddlers

Lopud is one of the Elaphiti Islands, northwest of Dubrovnik. The island has no cars, so toddlers can walk the village lanes and the waterfront promenade without traffic. The only motorised vehicles are small electric golf carts used as shuttles and for luggage.

The beaches are the main reason to come. Two small sandy beaches sit in the bay beside the ferry port. Šunj, on the south side, is the largest sandy beach in the Dubrovnik area. The sea there stays shallow far from shore, and children can wade about 100 m out before the water becomes deep. The slope is gentle enough that water shoes are not needed.

## How to Get to Lopud from Dubrovnik with Small Children

The Jadrolinija line 807 ferry leaves from Gruž port in Dubrovnik. It stops at Koločep, then Lopud, and then continues to Suđurađ on Šipan. The crossing takes 45–55 minutes. An adult ticket costs about €5, and the line carries foot passengers only.

The 2026 timetable gave these Monday–Saturday departures from Dubrovnik in the summer period (29 May–2 July and 31 August–27 September): 10:00, 14:00, 16:30 and 20:00. Lopud arrival is about 45 minutes later. Sunday and holiday times differ, with departures at 09:00, 11:45, 18:15 and 21:00. Timetables change by season and year, so check the 2027 schedule on the Jadrolinija website before booking.

**Return ferries are the main constraint.** In the 2026 summer timetable, the Monday–Saturday sailings from Lopud to Dubrovnik leave at about 06:10, 12:05 and 18:40. A day trip with a toddler needs to be planned around the 12:05 or 18:40 boat. The 18:40 sailing is the better choice because it leaves a full beach day and still gets a child to Dubrovnik in time for dinner.

Taxi boats and private speedboats from Dubrovnik take about 30 minutes. They cost much more than the ferry, but they avoid the Gruž queue in July and August.

## Getting Around Lopud with a Stroller or Toddler

The village and the harbour front are flat. The route to Šunj crosses the island over a hill, and the beach is 1.2–1.5 km from the port. Golf carts run between the village and the entrance to Šunj for €3 per person each way (2025 price). There is a stop at each end.

A pushchair looks practical for this island, but a soft carrier works better. The lanes to the old churches and the path to the Šunj bay are uneven in places, and stairs are common. A light stroller is enough for the promenade only. A carrier also helps a tired toddler on the walk back from the beach.

## Best Beaches on Lopud for Toddlers

### Šunj Beach
The sand is fine and grey-gold, and the water is clear and warm. It is south-facing, so it gets sun for most of the day. Facilities include toilets, changing cabins, showers and beach restaurants. A sunbed costs about €10 and an umbrella about €5 extra. Natural shade is limited, so bring a pop-up tent or a sun umbrella. Water temperature peaks at 24–26°C in August, and swimming is comfortable from June to October.

Šunj is popular and can be crowded between 11:00 and 16:00 in July and August. Arriving before 10:30 gives the best choice of spots near the shallow edge.

### Village Coves
The two small sandy beaches in the bay are only a few minutes from the ferry. Local children swim and play here. Pedalo and paddleboard hire is available, and there are cafés and an ice-cream bar nearby. These coves are the better choice for children under two. The toilets, food and the ferry are all within a short walk, and naps can happen back at the apartment.

## What to Do on Lopud Beyond the Beach

- **Walk the promenade.** The waterfront path is flat and shaded in places by pines and palms.
- **Visit the Franciscan monastery and the Kaštio fortress.** Both are in the village. The ruins are good for children who like climbing, but the steps and walls need close supervision.
- **Rent a bike.** Bikes are available in the village. Child seats should be requested in advance.
- **Try a kayak tour.** Tours leave from the bay beach, but they are better for children over about six.

## Where to Stay on Lopud with a Family

Accommodation is limited, so book early for July and August. Lafodia Hotel & Resort is the largest hotel on the island. Hotel Glavović sits on the village promenade. Private apartments and holiday houses make up the rest of the stock, and a kitchen helps with toddler mealtimes.

Choose a place in the village rather than near Šunj. The village has the ferry, shops and pharmacy within walking distance, and luggage can go by golf cart.

## Food, Supplies and Practical Tips

Lopud has small shops, but selection is limited. Bring nappies, wipes, sunscreen, baby food, and any specific formula from Dubrovnik. Buy them at a supermarket near Gruž port before boarding. Restaurants in the village and at Šunj serve simple dishes such as pasta, grilled fish and fries, which suit young children. Carry water to the beach in summer, because beach prices are higher.

**Local tips:**
- Take the first morning ferry out and the evening boat back to get the quieter beach hours.
- Keep cash for golf carts and small beach cafés, although many restaurants accept cards.
- There is no hospital on the island. Dubrovnik is a 45–55 minute ferry ride away, so carry a basic child medicine kit and any prescriptions.
- Late May, June and September have warm water, fewer crowds and a fuller ferry timetable than winter.

## Best Time to Visit

June and early September are the best months for toddlers. The sea is warm, Šunj is less crowded and the midday heat is easier to manage. July and August bring the highest temperatures and the most day-trip visitors. May is possible, but the water is cool for small children.

faq.question: Is Lopud good for toddlers?
faq.answer: Yes. The island has no car traffic, flat village lanes and shallow sandy beaches. Šunj Beach has water that stays shallow for about 100 m from shore. Limited shade and shops are the main drawbacks.

faq.question: How do you get to Lopud from Dubrovnik with children?
faq.answer: Take the Jadrolinija line 807 ferry from Gruž port. The crossing takes 45–55 minutes and a ticket costs about €5 per adult. The ferry carries foot passengers only, so strollers and luggage must be carried or wheeled aboard.

faq.question: How far is Šunj Beach from the Lopud ferry port?
faq.answer: Šunj is about 1.2–1.5 km from the port across the island. Golf carts run between the village and the beach for €3 per person each way. Walking takes about 20–30 minutes with a toddler.

faq.question: Can you use a stroller on Lopud?
faq.answer: A stroller works on the village promenade and flat lanes. It is less practical on the stairs and uneven paths toward Šunj and the fortress. A baby carrier is the more reliable option.

faq.question: Can you visit Lopud as a day trip with a toddler?
faq.answer: Yes, but the return ferry times limit the day. In the 2026 summer timetable, boats back to Dubrovnik left at about 12:05 and 18:40 on Monday to Saturday. The 18:40 sailing allows a full beach day.

faq.question: When is the best time to take young children to Lopud?
faq.answer: June and early September are the best months. The sea is warm, the heat is manageable and Šunj is less crowded than in July and August. Water is warmest in August at 24–26°C.

quickAnswer: Lopud suits families with toddlers because it has no cars, a shallow sandy beach at Šunj, and small sandy coves beside the village. The Jadrolinija ferry from Dubrovnik takes 45–55 minutes and costs about €5 per adult. Golf carts (€3 per person each way) cover the 1.2–1.5 km to Šunj. Shade and shops are limited.
